summary.prose: Building s2 turns the single-threaded daemon into a router with three workers: an admin worker that answers status and the TUI's reads from a shared status board, a code-indexing worker that owns the whole index queue, the watcher and every indexing method, and a document-summary worker that runs summaries only while code indexing is idle. The work starts with mechanical seams that change no behaviour (the handler runtime as a function, the method-class table, the server's forward seam, the contract amendments), then brings up each worker behind daemon.threads.enabled, adds one supervisor that recovers a crashed worker and releases its locks, and finishes with idle maintenance compaction under the daemon.maintenance lock. Session methods stay on the main thread until s3; every response stays wire-identical, and threads are switched on by default only after the end-to-end and smoke checks pass.

tasks.title: Main-thread thread services and the worker request entry
tasks.summary: Behind daemon.threads.enabled (a config schema key, default off until t17) the main thread creates the guard block, the lock block (installLockManager), the hub serving the board, step-state, store-health and target-registry services, a daemon.info hub op ({startedAt, modelState, installedCommit, lmdbFileSizeMb, maintenance?}) and an 'embedder.backend' push after bootstrapEmbeddingModel decides. A generic worker request entry, used by every s2 worker, dispatches RequestEnvelopes to the worker's tables with today's dispatch rules, relays frames, honours CancelEnvelope, answers a DataCloneError with a named error, and exposes a test hook reporting the serving thread id. tasks.title: Extensible worker supervisor and shutdown with workers
tasks.summary: One supervisor on the main thread, built so s4 can register the session workers with it: every started worker is registered with the lock framework's watchWorker; on a worker's exit it runs StoreGuard.reclaim, unregisters the target, fails that worker's in-flight requests with "the daemon's <class> thread stopped while serving <method>; retry", and starts a replacement (requests wait for it up to 30 s); restarts are limited to 5 in 60 s, past which it logs fatal and runs shutdown. A dead summary worker makes the code-indexing worker's remote processor reject that job; a dead code-indexing worker makes the summary worker abandon its job, and the new code-indexing worker restarts from the persisted registry. Shutdown: stopBackgroundWork stops each worker, queueDone settles on the code-indexing worker's drain or exit, closeStores closes the stores on the main thread after the workers exit; the locks-lost branch is unchanged.

tasks.title: Daemon maintenance lock at every entry point
tasks.summary: Every top-level request except daemon.status and daemon.compact takes 'daemon.maintenance' shared with ifAvailable at its entry (the router for main-thread session work, the worker request entry otherwise) and holds it until it finishes; when refused it is answered {error: "daemon busy: <activity> since <time> (<reason>); retry later"} from the holder's metadata and nothing runs. Nested in-daemon calls and underHold cross-class requests do not request it again. The prune and todo-retention timers, the watcher path and every indexing job take it shared with a bounded wait; understanding.watch and todos.subscribe take it per refresh with ifAvailable and skip during maintenance; getGraphStore on any thread other than the compactor rejects with MaintenanceInProgress while maintenance compacts.

tasks.title: Maintenance controller and daemon.compact through it
tasks.summary: On the main thread: idle detection (no non-admin request arriving or in flight for idleMs, default 30 min, and both lanes idle; admin polls do not count), the reclaimable estimate (file size minus pages in use from getStats over every named database) with both thresholds (25% and 256 MB), the exclusive request on 'daemon.maintenance' with metadata {activity:'compaction', reason} and the pause limit (10 min); the idle time, thresholds and pause limit are config schema keys with these defaults. Once granted, 'graph.close' to every live worker and their acknowledgements, compactGraphStore with a beforeRename check built from the acknowledgements, then release. Each decision is logged. daemon.compact on the code-indexing worker keeps today's busy refusal and otherwise asks the main thread to run maintenance now, returning its CompactResult (or the not-idle-in-time error); daemon.status reports maintenance from LockManager.query. Maintenance never starts unless store health is ok; a shutdown during maintenance waits for it or the hard-exit backstop.
